name: Geometry
notes: Shapes only. Level n holds n stars arranged in a recognisable figure, so the picture tells you the equation. Every level here carries NO objects and NO solutions on purpose: the geometry is authored, and the answers, the goals and the machinery each level needs are still open. Coordinates are snapped to the quarter unit the studio snaps to; the regular shapes sit on a circumcircle of radius 4 (the star on 4.5 and 1.75), and no vertex is more than a quarter unit off it against a 0.77 star hitbox. Score and equation goals are written from the shape’s own equation and are the first thing to re-tune once the answers exist. A closed shape cannot be entered from outside, so every ring level spawns the ball inside it, off the vertical axis so it does not balance.

levels.name: One
levels.intent: One star, so the shape is a point and the answer is whatever line reaches it. The pack opens by saying what it is: the stars are the picture, and the picture is the equation.

levels.name: Two
levels.intent: Two stars are a line, and a line is one equation. Goal 30 is a sloped line; a level line would be 20 but cannot move the ball on its own.

levels.name: Triangle
levels.intent: A 60-60-60 triangle, point down, on a circle of radius 4. Its three vertices sit exactly on one parabola (y = 0.49x² − 4), which is why this one is point down and why the goal is a single quadratic. Plain gravity, no billiard.

levels.name: Square
levels.intent: Four corners. They lie on one circle (x² + y² = 18), but a ball under plain gravity settles at the bottom of a closed curve rather than lapping it — measured at 4/8 on a square billiard — so the goal assumes two curves: something to catch the lower pair and something for the upper. Retune it to 40/1 if one curve turns out to do it.

levels.name: Pentagon
levels.intent: From here the shapes are regular and their vertices are all one circumcircle of radius 4, so the intended answer is x² + y² = 16 — one quadratic, 40. The spawn is inside the ring, which is where a lapping run has to start: a closed curve cannot be entered from outside.

levels.name: Cube
levels.intent: Six stars: the silhouette of a cube stood on a corner, which is a regular hexagon with two vertical sides. Same circumcircle of radius 4 as the pentagon, so the same single equation — the shape changes, the answer does not, which is the joke.

levels.name: Heptagon
levels.intent: Seven, the first shape with no tidy coordinates at all. Every vertex is still within a quarter of a unit of the radius-4 circle, and the star hitbox is 0.77, so the circle still fits them comfortably.

levels.name: Three in a row
levels.intent: Eight stars as three squares of side 3 sharing their edges — a 2 × 4 grid. The shape breaks the run of circles: two horizontal rows, so two equations. Goal 60 is two sloped lines; two constants would be 40, since a constant costs nothing, and that is the level’s real prize if a flat track can be made to carry the ball.

levels.name: Nine
levels.intent: Nine evenly around the radius-4 circle — the pack’s cleanest statement of its own rule. One equation, and the only question is how to keep the ball going round.

levels.name: The star
levels.intent: Ten: the five outer points and five inner corners of a five-pointed star. They sit on two concentric circles, radius 4.5 and radius 1.75 — the pentagram ratio — so the goal is two quadratics, 80. The spawn sits between the two rings.
